source_evidence.quote: In this case-control study, 30 diabetic subjects with angiographically defined CAD were compared with 30 age- and sex-matched diabetic subjects without CAD in terms of clinical and laboratory parameters including serum irisin levels.
A prospective cohort study was conducted at a tertiary referral hospital in Southern Brazil.

Patients were divided according to body mass index: Group 1 (body mass index = 18.5 - 29.9 kg/m2; n = 15), Group 2 (body mass index = 30 - 39.9 kg/m2; n = 36), and Group 3 (body mass index ≥ 40 kg/m2; n = 30).

verdict.label: apparent_contradiction
verdict.rationale: Both claims are correctly extracted and verified. Study A reports a significant positive correlation between serum irisin and BMI (r = 0.374, P = 0.004) in type II diabetic patients, while Study B reports a significant negative correlation between irisin and waist circumference (r = -0.272, p = 0.024) and with weight (r = -0.246), plus lower irisin in the highest-BMI group. These are genuinely opposite directions for the irisin-adiposity association. The abstracts provide concrete, text-supported contextual differences that could explain the discrepancy: A is a case-control study restricted to type II diabetic patients with or without angiographically defined CAD, whereas B is a prospective cohort in Southern Brazil of predominantly obese patients stratified by BMI and undergoing cholecystectomy or gastric bypass. The anthropometric measures also differ (BMI in A vs waist circumference/weight in B), as does the biosample (serum vs plasma). These source-supported differences justify apparent_contradiction rather than contradictory.
